title: Bench feasibility test for the SNAP25 myasthenic hypothesis

sentences.text: This is a hypothesis, not a finding; its weakest link is the pathway argument and the unresolved distinction between neuromuscular and central SNAP25 presentations.
Test whether an acetylcholinesterase inhibitor improves neuromuscular function in a suitable laboratory model of the myasthenic presentation.
Human neurons derived from patient hiPSCs carrying SNAP25 V48F are described, with increased spontaneous release.
Use these only for an initial release-focused assessment; do not assume they establish a neuromuscular-junction model.
Before drug testing, ask the lab to identify a suitable cellular or animal neuromuscular model and measurement method; if unavailable, these would need to be built and validated.
Predefine measurements of spontaneous release and neuromuscular function before and after inhibitor exposure, keeping variant-specific results separate.
Plan matched untreated comparisons and a reference without the tested SNAP25 variant, subject to model availability.

sections.heading: What result would change the plan

sentences.text: Proceed only if a reproducible neuromuscular deficit can be measured; improvement would support further bench testing, while no improvement or worsening would argue against this approach in that model.
The graph contains no study testing this therapy class in SNAP25-related disease and no evidence establishing the required direction of pathway correction.
Do not generalize a model result across SNAP25 variants or to patients.
